kill_argument: Beyond Kling's (2001) exact replication, the paper sells two things: inference robust to a weak instrument and to a direct effect, and a process checked against its own ledger. Neither holds as written. The only test that bears on Card's basic specification is a projection set the design predicted would contain zero; it does, and the run shows why: the robust statistic at zero (7.30) is no smaller than the homoskedastic one (6.84), so the 'not established' comes largely from the chi-square(3) critical value, not from the data. Everything that comes out positive concerns a Panel A coefficient the paper itself says cannot equal the return. The process account fails on its own terms: the paper and AI-use statement say Card's SAS listing was opened only after every other claim was written, yet 34 result claims and one analysis run postdate it; the review counts double-count carried findings; the rerun has not run. What I attacked that held: every result number is a macro equal to its run, no claim value changed after the results gate, the H1 counts and named misses, the D4 and D7 labels, and the H3(b) and Panel A wording.

The paper says the SAS-listing comparison came 'only after every other claim was written' and 'After every other claim was written, a single report-only run compared the listing'; the AI-use statement says the listing 'was left unopened until every other claim was written'. check-sas-listing ran at 2026-11-20T19:11:59Z. The substance is intact: the 13 values come from metrics of runs made at 18:47-18:53Z, before the listing was read, and no claim value, support or macro changed after the results gate (I diffed claims.jsonl against commit 569bc72). Cheapest remedy, narrowing: 'after every claim of the approved plan was written; 13 claims taken from existing run metrics were added at the results review and 21 descriptive claims (D7) at the paper stage; no claim value changed after the listing was read'.

findings.text: Unit error in the abstract and elsewhere: 0.0114 is in units of log wage, i.e. about 1.1 log points, but the abstract, the introduction and Section 4.4 say proximity may raise log wages 'by 0.0114 log points', and Table 4 labels the breakdown '(log points)'. The paper contradicts itself two paragraphs later ('a direct effect of about one log point', also in the conclusion). Same error in Section 4.1: '0.1324 log points correspond to a 14.2% higher hourly wage' (0.1324 is 13.2 log points), introduced as 'In real units', which suggests inflation adjustment; it is a percent conversion of a point estimate whose robust set contains zero. Remedy: 'by 0.0114 (about 1.1 log points)' or 'by 0.0114 in log wage'; 'a coefficient of 0.1324 corresponds to a 14.2% wage difference'; fix the table label. The claim texts of a6-/a5-pacoef-chr-breakdown and plan.json H4 carry the same '(log points)' wording.

findings.text: Scope framing: the introduction's second question is 'how much of the IV conclusion survives inference that is robust to a weak instrument and to a bounded violation of the exclusion restriction', and the figure title is 'Sensitivity of the IV conclusions to a direct effect of college proximity'. The exclusion sensitivity exists only for the Panel A coefficient (D2); Card's basic specification gets only the weak-IV-robust set. The next paragraph clarifies, but the question as posed promises both for 'the IV conclusion' (the wording question-r2 F7 asked to change in the plan). Remedy: name the specifications in the question and the figure title.

findings.text: The H3(b) reading understates evidence already in the ledger. The paper says the robust set contains zero 'possibly because the projection is conservative'. h3b-subvector also wrote b6_kappap_at_zero = 6.836, the homoskedastic subvector AR statistic at b0 = 0 on the chi-square scale (it equals 3.841 at the GKMC bounds), against the robust profile statistic m(0) = 7.300. The robust statistic at zero is not smaller than the homoskedastic one, so the gap between the robust and homoskedastic decisions comes from the critical value (chi-square(3) vs chi-square(1) or GKM19), not from heteroskedasticity. Remedy: a report-only claim on the existing metric, labelled descriptive and post hoc. It must not change the H3(b) decision rule or its primary set.

findings.text: The title promises more than the text delivers in two ways. (a) 'Card's (1995)': the 1995 chapter was never read, and every target is a WP 4483 (1993) number (Limitations, Sources). (b) 'Does growing up near a college raise schooling and earnings?' is the first-stage and reduced-form question, which needs only proximity independence, not exclusion. The paper never answers it in those terms: it reports the reduced forms only as restatements of the AR and CHR results for the return. Remedy: name the working paper in the title (e.g. 'Card's (1993, 1995)'), and either answer the title question explicitly from the first-stage and reduced-form claims with their Panel A or B labels, or retitle.
